case: Maximum 63-byte PostgreSQL custom-enum scalar and array labels, including multibyte UTF-8
contract: A 63-byte ASCII label and a 21-character three-byte UTF-8 label are both preserved at the PostgreSQL enum label byte limit.
pg_enum.enumlabel and octet_length provide an independent catalog/value oracle for exact label bytes and the 63-byte boundary.
enum_range and pg_typeof confirm direct result decoding retains each exact label as the declared custom enum type without byte or character truncation.
The multibyte label also survives enum[] projection with a SQL NULL element; array_to_json checks element semantics and a bound array_send comparison confirms exact native bytes.
The decoded enum[] text quotes the label while native canonical array text does not; JSON semantics and wire equality confirm the representations are equivalent.
This proves the maximum accepted scalar/array label boundary; overlength declaration refusal and other enum consumer/session configurations are recorded separately or remain open.

native_contract.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres value_contract_custom_enum_preserves_maximum_multibyte_label_bytes -- --ignored --nocapture

clippy.command: rtk proxy cargo clippy --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres --all-targets -- -D warnings

remaining: Other enum operators, consumer formats, and session/search_path combinations remain open. The separate overlength-label manifest records the 64-byte refusal.
